profile.constituencyprofile_Text: The Kodumur Assembly Constituency initially formed in 1962 and restructured in 2008. The region's economy is predominantly agrarian, with agriculture serving as the mainstay for many residents. The fertile lands support the cultivation of various crops, contributing to the local economy. Additionally, the area has seen developments in renewable energy. The constituency has a rich historical and cultural heritage, with diverse geographical features and potential for economic growth. Its proximity to nearby towns like Kurnool, Adoni and Bellary makes it well-connected for trade, commerce, and tourism development.
profile.geography: Kodumur shares boundaries with the Kurnool, Yemmiganur, and Pattikonda constituencies, as well as Telangana State. The constituency is situated on the banks of the Tungabhadra River, a primary tributary of the Krishna River, enriching the region's agricultural potential. It is predominantly characterized by black cotton and red soils. Key water resources in the region include the Tungabhadra Project, Low Level Canal, Gajuladinne (Sanjeevaiah Sagar) Project, and K.C Canal, ensuring a steady supply for irrigation. The region is at an average elevation of 342 meters above sea level and receives an average annual rainfall of 641.2 mm, primarily from the South-West Monsoon, although drought conditions can occur when the monsoon fails.
profile.populationDesc: Kodumur constituency has a total population of 2,45,295 with 70% residing in rural areas and 30% in urban areas. The constituency has 52,732 households, with a sex ratio of 983 females per 1,000 males. The literacy rate stands at 52.36%.
profile.administrationDesc: Kodumur Constituency is one of the seven assembly constituencies in Kurnool district. It includes Kodumur, Gudur, C Belagal and some parts of Kurnool rural mandal.
profile.educationHealthcareDesc: Kodumur is a major educational hub, home to Kurnool, Viswabharathi Medical College, G Pulla reddy Engineering College, Pullaiah Engineering College, and Rayalaseema University.  The healthcare sector includes 13 PHCs, 35 sub-centers, 1 CHCs with plans to reduce maternal mortality by 50%, bring infant mortality below 10 per 1,000 live births, and achieve 100% vaccination coverage.
profile.culturalheritageDesc: Kodumur is known for its rich cultural and spiritual heritage, with key attractions such as Gorantla Madhava Swamy Temple, Krishnadoddi Venkateswara Swamy Temple, Kodumur Vallelamba Temple and K. Nagalapuram Sunkula Parameswari Temple. The handloom industry is a significant contributor to the economy, with Kodumur Handloom Sarees being GI tagged and widely exported.

economy_text.economy_Text:
The Economic Vision Plan for Kodumur (2024–2029) aims to transform the constituency into a vibrant, inclusive, and sustainable economic hub by leveraging its strengths in agriculture (36.04% of GCVA), industry (28.57%), and services (35.39%) to achieve a projected GCDP growth from ₹5,540 crores in 2023-24 to ₹11,568 crores by 2028-29, with per capita income rising from ₹1,88,070 to ₹3,83,121. 

Key growth drivers include agricultural modernization through irrigation and crop diversification, industrial expansion via MSMEs and renewable energy, and service sector growth in IT, tourism, and financial inclusion. 

Strategic thrust areas focus on sustainable infrastructure, skill development, economic diversification, and alignment with Swarna Andhra 2047, positioning Kodumur for long-term resilience and prosperity.
economy_text.gcdP_Growth_Text: By 2029, Kodumur will transition from an agriculture-dominated constituency to a balanced, diversified economy, with thrust on horticulture, MSMEs, construction, renewable energy, financial services, and digital infrastructure

thrust.description: Development of IT parks, digital services, and start-up incubation hubs.
High-yield fruit, vegetable, and floriculture production with cold chain and export linkages.
Support for MSMEs and large manufacturers across sectors through enabling industrial policies.
